title: Relay Studio Help
introduction: Use Relay Studio to design REST requests, run multi-step flows, save response evidence, and diagnose failures without sending project data to a hosted workspace.

sections.title: Projects
sections.body: Projects are local .restproj files containing requests, flows, environments, variables, and workspace settings.
steps: Create or open a project from File or the command palette.
Use Save Project As to choose its first location.
Keep credentials out of project values; use approved local-only configuration for secrets.

sections.title: Requests
sections.body: Select a request in Explorer, choose its method, URL, authorization, headers, parameters, body, retry policy, and timeout, then select Send Request.
steps: Choose the intended environment before sending.
Review status, headers, timing, body, and console diagnostics.
In a formatted JSON response, select a same-origin HTTP(S) URL to create a new GET request with the source request's authorization settings.
Use Cancel Request to stop an in-progress request.

sections.title: Flows
sections.body: Flows connect requests into ordered success and failure paths with response mappings and assertions.
steps: Add request steps and connect their success or failure paths.
Map earlier response values into variables needed by later steps.
Run the flow, inspect each step, and use Cancel Flow when necessary.

sections.title: Code Examples
sections.body: Generate local, read-only HTTP, cURL, C#, Java, jQuery, Node.js, PHP, Python, or Ruby examples from an open request or flow without sending it.
steps: Right-click a request or flow tab, choose Generate Code, then choose a language.
Review safe credential and multipart-file placeholders, switch languages if needed, and choose Copy Code.

For flows, implement the generated branch prerequisites before running the example; Java and jQuery output capture and reuse mapped JSON response values automatically. Java mapping output requires Jackson Databind, requires credential masks such as <REDACTED> to be supplied securely at runtime, and fails actionably for non-2xx, empty, malformed JSON, missing, null, or non-scalar mapping responses.

sections.title: Saved Responses
sections.body: Save response artifacts for offline evidence and reopen them from Explorer.
steps: Choose a JSON or text destination.
Confirm explicitly before overwriting an existing artifact.
Verify sensitive headers and values are redacted before sharing.

sections.title: Recovery And Backups
sections.body: Relay Studio validates project schema, uses atomic native saves, and keeps recovery backups for the last valid project state.
steps: Follow the recovery guidance shown when a project is invalid.
Restore the backup only when the primary file cannot be opened.
Do not edit the primary project concurrently in multiple Relay Studio windows.

sections.title: Diagnostics And Security
sections.body: Diagnostics export includes application, platform, project counts, and recent console context with known secrets redacted.
steps: Export diagnostics from Settings > Workspace.
Inspect the generated JSON before sharing it.
Never include passwords, bearer tokens, cookies, API keys, or private project data in issue reports.

sections.title: Keyboard And Navigation
sections.body: The native menus and command palette expose the same primary workspace actions.
steps: Open command search with Cmd+K on macOS or Ctrl+K on Windows and Linux.
Save with Cmd+S or Ctrl+S and send or run with Cmd+Enter or Ctrl+Enter.
Use the View menu to toggle Explorer, Inspector, Response Dock, and Flow Details.
